topic: Will we be able to predict catastrophic weather events more accurately?
research_question: At a fixed information and communication budget, can hazard-specific hybrid models plus a shared calibration-and-decision layer improve probabilistic skill and warning utility over physics-only, AI-only, and uncalibrated ensemble baselines?

candidate_routes.name: universal_multimodal_model
candidate_routes.reason: risks conflating distinct physical dynamics and observation processes

candidate_routes.name: independent_best_in_class_models
candidate_routes.reason: respects hazard physics but omits shared calibration and end_to_end warning utility

candidate_routes.name: hazard_specific_modules_shared_calibration
candidate_routes.reason: preserves physical separation while addressing uncertainty, latency, and decision gaps

falsifiable_claims: calibration improves weighted probabilistic score and reliability at matched information cutoffs
latency-aware decisions improve lead time or impact-weighted regret at a fixed false-alert budget
removing physical constraints, latency gating, or calibration causes hazard-specific degradation
cross-hazard transfer helps representation and calibration but does not require shared physical transition parameters
required_boundaries: tsunami warning begins after source initiation
forecast skill is distinct from warning utility
